skill.name: firefox-browser
skill.description: Operate a live Firefox browser session through a local browser CLI, including tabs, navigation, page content, forms, screenshots, JavaScript, and optional Bitwarden login.
skill.summary: Automate a live Firefox session with real cookies, tabs, page interaction, screenshots, JavaScript, and optional credential filling.
skill.author: 1jehuang

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, and the hardcoded URLs are examples. Real risks remain because the skill invokes a local browser CLI, starts Firefox in the background, and captures screenshots. It controls an authenticated Firefox profile, can use Bitwarden credentials, can execute arbitrary page JavaScript, and shows no prompt injection evidence.

remediation.suggestion: Default to a separate browser profile or require explicit confirmation before reading tabs, private pages, screenshots, or authenticated content.
Remove automatic vault unlock and auto-submit, or require visible per-domain approval before filling or submitting credentials.
Disable evaluate and pageWorld access by default, or restrict them to user-approved scripts with secret redaction.
Gate screenshots and page extraction behind explicit user consent and redact sensitive form values when possible.
Avoid nohup startup in the skill instructions, or document how users can inspect and stop the background browser process.

content.value_statement: AI agents often need the same authenticated browser state that users already have. This skill connects Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to Firefox for guided web automation.
actual_capabilities: List open Firefox tabs and create new browser sessions.
Navigate pages and extract text, HTML, or annotated content.
Click elements, type text, fill forms, wait for content, and scroll pages.
Capture visible page screenshots as PNG files.
Execute JavaScript in isolated or page-world contexts.
Auto-fill credentials from a Bitwarden-backed vault when configured.
limitations: Requires Firefox, the browser bridge, and the browser CLI to be installed and running.
Uses the real Firefox profile, so actions can affect active accounts and sessions.
Cannot bypass site permissions, CAPTCHAs, multi-factor authentication, or access controls.
Screenshots, page content, and form values can expose private information.

use_cases.title: Test Authenticated Web Flows
use_cases.description: Use a real Firefox session to inspect pages, click controls, fill forms, and verify user-facing flows.

use_cases.title: Collect Web Page Details
use_cases.description: Open pages, read annotated content, compare page text, and capture visible evidence when needed.

use_cases.title: Assist Account Workflows
use_cases.description: Navigate logged-in pages, check form states, and complete routine browser tasks with user oversight.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Current Browser State
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the open Firefox tabs, identify the active tab, and suggest which tab is safest to use for this task.

prompt_templates.title: Read a Web Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the provided page in a new Firefox session, read the annotated content, and summarize the main interactive elements.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Form With Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Fill the named fields on this page, stop before submitting, and show me what values will be sent.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Use isolated Firefox tabs to compare these pages, extract the relevant differences, and avoid using credentials unless I approve.

output_examples.input: Inspect the active Firefox session before starting work.
output_examples.output: The response lists the open windows and tabs, names the active page, and recommends using a new session for isolation.

output_examples.input: Read a product page and identify available actions.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes visible product details, prices, form fields, links, and buttons that can be clicked.

output_examples.input: Fill a support form but do not submit it.
output_examples.output: The response confirms each filled field, reports any missing selector, and pauses for user approval before submission.

best_practices: Start with a new session or explicit tab ID to avoid changing unrelated browser tabs.
Ask for user approval before using credentials, submitting forms, or capturing private pages.
Use annotated content before clicking so selectors and form states are visible.
anti_patterns: Do not use auto-login or auto-submit without clear user authorization.
Do not run arbitrary JavaScript on untrusted pages unless the user approved the exact purpose.
Do not capture screenshots of sensitive pages unless the task requires visible evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill use my real Firefox profile?
faq.answer: Yes. It controls the live Firefox browser and can use existing cookies, tabs, and authenticated sessions.

faq.question: What must be installed before use?
faq.answer: Firefox, the browser bridge extension, the native host, and the browser CLI must be available.

faq.question: Can it fill passwords automatically?
faq.answer: It can use Bitwarden-backed credential filling when the local vault integration is configured.

faq.question: Can it take screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents a screenshot action that captures the visible page area as a PNG file.

faq.question: Can it run JavaScript on pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run evaluation scripts with DOM access, including page-world access when requested.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive accounts?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill can view private pages, fill credentials, submit forms, and capture visible account data.
